newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Hindu party to form government in key state.
newsitem.headline: Indian Hindu party to form government in key state.

text.p: India's rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said on Wednesday it had reached an agreement with an influential party of lower-caste Hindus to form a government in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
India's most populous state has been ruled directly by New Delhi after inconclusive local elections in September last year failed to yield a clear majority for any one political group.

A BJP spokesman told Reuters that under Wednesday's agreement his party would allow the rival Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) to head the two-party coaliton government for six months, followed by a six-month turn at the helm by the BJP.
"Every six months we will change the party to head the government," the spokesman said. "The first government will be headed by the BSP."

Wednesday's decision followed angry protests in parliament by the BJP which has demanded the dismissal of Uttar Pradesh governor Romesh Bhandari, saying he was responsible for a spurt in crime in the state.
